claim: speech-front skips unit expansion (млн, кг, км, тыс.) on decimal numbers due to `!decimal` guard.
invariant: Decimal quantities with known Russian unit abbreviations must expand and decline the unit into genitive singular.
reason: Verified in speech-front/src/normalize.rs:460 (`if !decimal`) vs teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:544 (`decimal_with_suffix`), and reproduced via CLI (`2.5 млн` -> `две целых пять десятых млн`).
counterevidence: Percentage (`%`) on decimals is handled separately at line 453; integer units work normally.

claim: speech-front lacks `parse_iso_date`, corrupting YYYY-MM-DD dates into hyphenated numeric ranges plus `-DD`.
invariant: ISO-8601 dates must normalize as calendar dates (or preserve ISO datetimes), never split into ranges.
reason: Verified in speech-front/src/normalize.rs:214-221 (missing `parse_iso_date`) vs teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:373-445, and reproduced via CLI (`2026-08-12` -> `две тысячи двадцать шесть — восемь-двенадцать`).
counterevidence: Dot/slash numeric dates (`DD.MM.YYYY`) are handled by `parse_numeric_date`.

claim: speech-front expands leading numbers of hyphenated technical identifiers (`64-bit`, `12-factor`, `7-zip`).
invariant: Numbers attached to hyphenated technical identifier tails must remain untouched.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/normalize.rs:443 (missing `followed_by_identifier_tail` from teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:527,883) and reproduced via CLI (`64-bit` -> `шестьдесят четыре-bit`).
counterevidence: Preceding identifiers like `x86_64` are guarded by `attached_to_identifier`.

claim: speech-front `parse_version` omits `attached_to_identifier`, rewriting `node-v22.23.2` into `node-вэ двадцать два...`.
invariant: Version strings attached to hyphenated package names must not be expanded in isolation.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/normalize.rs:258 vs teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:264 and reproduced via CLI.
counterevidence: Direct alphanumeric prefixes without hyphens are blocked by `previous_is_identifier`.

claim: teratts-server `boundaries_match` dropped the leading-dot guard (`first == Some('.')`), allowing `.NET` to match after `/` or `-` if added to lexicon.
invariant: Punctuation-prefixed lexicon entries must not match inside URL paths or hyphenated tokens.
reason: Verified in diff between speech-front/src/normalize.rs:188-193 and teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:195-201.
counterevidence: `.NET` is not currently in production `lexicon.toml`; `example.NET` is still blocked by `!previous.is_some_and(is_identifier_char)`.

claim: speech-front `boundaries_match` permits non-identifier-prefixed entries like `/v1/chat/completions` to match immediately after domain names (`example.com/v1/chat/completions`).
invariant: Lexicon entries starting with `/` must not match when immediately preceded by an identifier character.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/normalize.rs:194 (`!first.is_some_and(is_identifier_char)` is true for `'/'`, bypassing `!previous.is_some_and(...)`) and reproduced via CLI (`https://example.comви один, чат комплишнс`).
counterevidence: teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:199 already fixed this by requiring `!previous.is_some_and(is_identifier_char)`.

claim: speech-front `longest_match` allocates two `String`s (`to_lowercase()`) and recounts chars per entry per char position.
invariant: Hot-path lexicon scanning should avoid per-character heap allocations.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/normalize.rs:166-168 vs teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:103-116,173-182 which precomputes `written_lower` and `written_char_count`.
counterevidence: Input length in CLI/review usage is bounded and `teratts-server` already uses the zero-allocation version.

claim: `LexiconReload::refresh` holds `self.state.lock()` while reading up to 2 MiB from disk, computing SHA-256, and parsing TOML.
invariant: Snapshot mutex should only be held or contended minimally, or unchanged files should skip full read+hash.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/lexicon_reload.rs:56-65.
counterevidence: `teratts-server` admits at most 1 active synthesis + 2 waiting requests, and `TERATTS_LEXICON_PATH` is unset by default (using builtin in-memory lexicon).

claim: Hardcoded `0x800` for `O_NONBLOCK` on Linux is non-portable to SPARC/MIPS/Alpha.
invariant: File open flags must be valid on supported deployment targets.
reason: Rejected as a defect: deployment target is explicitly x86_64 Debian 12 LXC (`docs/speech-front-integration.md:77-79`), and avoiding a direct `libc` crate dependency for one constant is intentional.
counterevidence: Inline comment at lines 131-132 explicitly documents the Linux UAPI constant and scope.

claim: When an external lexicon file is corrupted, `LexiconReload::refresh` re-reads, re-hashes, and re-parses the broken TOML on every enabled request.
invariant: Unchanged invalid lexicon files should not be repeatedly parsed on every request.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/lexicon_reload.rs:59-64: `state.revision` only updates on `Ok`, so a bad file triggers `parse(&bytes)` every time.
counterevidence: Diagnostic logging is throttled to 60s, and valid snapshot fallback is preserved.

claim: `parse_numeric_date` and `parse_iso_date` do not consume trailing `года`/`год`/`г.`, producing duplicate `года года` or `года г.`.
invariant: Calendar date normalizers must consume optional following year suffixes (`optional_year_suffix`) just like `parse_text_date`.
reason: Verified in `speech-front/src/normalize.rs:347-362` and `teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:354-371,405-422`, and reproduced via CLI (`12.08.2026 года` -> `...две тысячи двадцать шестого года года`).
counterevidence: `parse_text_date` (`6 августа 2026 года`) already calls `optional_year_suffix`.

claim: Numeric range branch in `parse_number` only expands `%` suffixes and leaves standard unit suffixes (`10-20 км`) unexpanded.
invariant: Numeric ranges followed by unit abbreviations should decline the unit using the right-hand bound.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:481-491 and speech-front/src/normalize.rs:398-408, and reproduced via CLI (`10-20 км` -> `десять — двадцать км`).
counterevidence: Single numbers (`20 км`) and percentage ranges (`10-15%`) expand units normally.

claim: `teratts-server` `flatten_tags` converts non-2-letter angle-bracket tags (`<b>`, `<div>`, `<path>`) into spoken words (`div`, `path`), whereas `speech-front` rejects all unknown `<tag>` markup.
invariant: Cross-repo `russian-only` tag handling should either share a documented placeholder contract or reject HTML tags consistently.
reason: Verified in teratts-server/src/russian_only.rs:408-425 (added in commit 70d95e2 to allow LLM placeholders like `<path>`) vs speech-front/src/russian_only.rs:260-265.
counterevidence: Commit 70d95e2 intentionally allowed `<placeholder>` in `teratts-server` for LLM output resilience, though HTML tags like `<div>` also become spoken words and `speech-front` lacks this rule.

claim: `teratts-server` `normalize_symbols` replaces precomposed Latin letters with diacritics, ligatures, and fullwidth Latin (`café`, `ﬂow`, `ＡＰＩ`) with spaces before calling `speech-front`.
invariant: Latin characters supported by `speech-front`'s `latin(c)` NFKD deaccenting contract must not be stripped into spaces by `teratts-server`.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/russian_only.rs:303,335: only `c.is_ascii_alphabetic()` is permitted for Latin, whereas speech-front/src/russian_only.rs:348-352 supports `0x00C0..=0x024F` (except `×,÷,ß,ø`), `0x1E00..=0x1EFF`, `0xFB00..=0xFB06`, `0xFF21..=0xFF5A`. Thus `café` becomes `caf ` instead of `кафе`/`кэйф`.
counterevidence: Commit d273224 intended to replace unsupported CJK/emoji with spaces, but inadvertently excluded non-ASCII Latin ranges supported by `speech-front`.

claim: `speech-front` prints up to `MAX_SERIALIZED_BYTES` (262,144) with `println!` (+1 byte `\n`), which exceeds `teratts-server`'s `MAX_JSON_BYTES` (262,144) by 1 byte at the exact boundary.
invariant: Subprocess framing must account for the trailing newline emitted by `println!`.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/main.rs:122 (`println!`) vs teratts-server/src/russian_only.rs:195-204 (`bytes.len() > MAX_JSON_BYTES`).
counterevidence: Requires a conversion output of exactly 262,144 bytes, which is unreachable for typical TTS utterances.

claim: `speech-front russian-only` CLI pre-strips `<ru>/<en>` tags at line 114 before `Converter::convert`, suppressing the `language_tags_removed` warning.
invariant: CLI `russian-only` output should include `language_tags_removed` in `warnings` when `<ru>/<en>` tags were stripped, matching `Converter::convert`.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/main.rs:114 and reproduced via CLI (`printf '<en>API</en>' | speech-front russian-only` outputs `warnings: ['automatic_not_approved']` without `language_tags_removed`).
counterevidence: Downstream `teratts-server` does not inspect the `language_tags_removed` warning string.

claim: `teratts-server` spawns the `speech-front` subprocess and opens SQLite `cmudict.db` on every `russian_only` request even when the text is already 100% valid Russian plaintext.
invariant: Pure Cyrillic requests in `russian_only` mode that already satisfy `valid_plaintext` need no subprocess fork or SQLite lookup.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/server.rs:904-913 and teratts-server/src/russian_only.rs:150-256.
counterevidence: Local subprocess + SQLite open takes only a few milliseconds on Linux, well within TTS synthesis latency (~500-1500 ms).

claim: Duplicate of G1-08: `LexiconReload::refresh` locks mutex and reads/hashes `lexicon.toml` on every request.
invariant: Unchanged lexicon files should not cause synchronous disk read + SHA-256 under a global lock on every request.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/lexicon_reload.rs:53-66; root-cause duplicate of G1-08.
counterevidence: Only active when `TERATTS_LEXICON_PATH` is explicitly configured.

claim: When `speech-front` rejects input for `reading_limit_exceeded` (>1024 readings) or `output_limit_exceeded` (>12,000 chars), `teratts-server` maps the non-zero exit to `ConversionError::Failed` (HTTP 502) instead of `InvalidText` (HTTP 400).
invariant: Client input expansion limit violations should map to HTTP 400 Bad Request rather than HTTP 502 Bad Gateway.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/russian_only.rs:161,232-235 and src/server.rs:1164-1166.
counterevidence: Input character count and character set are already pre-validated in `teratts-server` before spawning the child.

claim: `split_term` in `render.rs` does not split same-case Cyrillic/Latin transitions (`ТЕСТAPI`), so `Generator::suggest` misses script boundaries that `russian_only.rs` pre-splits.
invariant: Compound splitter in `render.rs` should split script transitions consistently across both `russian_only` and `suggest`.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/pronounce/render.rs:125-135 vs speech-front/src/russian_only.rs:156-174.
counterevidence: `observe::detect` marks mixed-script tokens as `suspected-typo`, so they rarely enter the normal `suggest` review flow.

claim: Ponytail ceiling breached: comment states `162 entries are tiny; use a sorted scan`, while `lexicon.toml` now has 186 entries.
invariant: Documented ponytail ceilings should be updated or revisited when the threshold is crossed.
reason: Verified via `grep -c '^\[\[entry\]\]' lexicon.toml` == 186 and `speech-front/src/normalize.rs:93`.
counterevidence: 186 entries is only 14.8% above 162; linear scan with precomputed lowercase (once G1-07 is ported) remains microsecond-scale.

claim: Duplicate of G3-01 in vendored `teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs`: `162 entries` ponytail comment vs 186 actual entries.
invariant: Documented ponytail ceilings should match current lexicon size.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:94; duplicate root cause of G3-01.
counterevidence: `teratts-server` already uses zero-allocation iterator matching.

claim: Ponytail marker `// ponytail: bounded beam of three candidates per part, not a full Cartesian product.` lacks an explicit upgrade trigger (`no-trigger`).
invariant: Every `ponytail:` marker must name both its ceiling and its upgrade trigger.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/pronounce/mod.rs:152. Note: G3's sub-claim that the beam is unpruned was refuted by coordinator inspection of `dedup(&mut next)` at line 409 (`unique.truncate(LIMIT)`), which DOES prune to 3 candidates per part; only the `no-trigger` comment tag is confirmed.
counterevidence: `dedup(&mut next)` at lines 235 and 409 properly enforces `LIMIT = 3`.

claim: Ponytail marker `// ponytail: kill only this process; binaries spawning descendants are unsupported.` lacks an upgrade trigger (`no-trigger`).
invariant: Every `ponytail:` comment should specify when to revisit the shortcut.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/russian_only.rs:153.
counterevidence: `speech-front russian-only` is a single-process synchronous binary that never spawns child processes.

claim: `observe.rs` (2137 LOC, including 789 LOC of tests) combines SQLite persistence, Horizon TSV/JSON import, atomic lexicon locking, and text token classification.
invariant: Cohesive module separation improves maintainability as `speech-front` grows.
reason: Verified line counts and responsibility boundaries in `speech-front/src/observe.rs`.
counterevidence: 1,348 lines of production Rust in one module is self-contained and well-tested (49 tests pass).

claim: `GitPublisher` (100 LOC) is embedded inside the Axum HTTP review module `review.rs` (1067 LOC).
invariant: Separating Git CLI automation from HTTP route handlers improves modularity.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/review.rs:343-442.
counterevidence: `GitPublisher` is only used by `review::serve` and is under 100 lines.

claim: 1,166 lines of normalization logic in `teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs` duplicate `speech-front/src/normalize.rs` (1,003 LOC), directly causing the 6 behavioral drift bugs found in G1-01..G1-07.
invariant: Shared normalization logic should be maintained in one authoritative source or synchronized mechanically.
reason: Verified via `check-4-cross-repo-diff.txt` (646-line diff between the two copies) and the resulting drift bugs G1-01..G1-07.
counterevidence: The two repositories have different licenses (`speech-front` vs GPL-3.0 `teratts-server`, noted in `docs/speech-front-integration.md:82-83`), which originally motivated vendoring.

claim: `speech-front serve --tera-url` sets `RendererCommand` to re-invoke `speech-front render-tera` as a child process instead of calling `tera_client::render` in-process.
invariant: In-process rendering avoids redundant process spawn and double WAV validation.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/main.rs:76-88 and src/review.rs:316-339.
counterevidence: Reusing `RendererCommand` unifies the codepath with external Python renderers, and preview clicks are manual human actions.

claim: A 0-byte `.speech-front.lock` file left by a crash between `create_new` and `write_all(MARKER)` blocks subsequent approvals with `foreign or incomplete lexicon lock file`.
invariant: Lock files must never blindly overwrite unknown or incomplete files.
reason: Rejected as a bug: `observe::tests::foreign_lock_file_is_never_overwritten` (`observe.rs:178`) explicitly requires that any lockfile without `MARKER` (including 0-byte files) be rejected rather than overwritten.
counterevidence: Covered by explicit unit test `foreign_lock_file_is_never_overwritten` in `check-1-speech-front-test.txt`.

claim: Preview audio cache filenames use `{pid}-{sequence}.wav` (`review.rs:270`) while `RendererCommand::render` (`review.rs:319`) errors if the target file already exists; if a restarted server reuses the same PID (e.g. PID 1 in a container or recycled OS PID), preview fails with HTTP 502.
invariant: Preview cache filenames must not collide across server restarts into a persistent `--audio-cache` directory.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/review.rs:269-271 and 318-320.
counterevidence: On bare-metal host OSes without fixed container PIDs, PID reuse across restarts is infrequent.

claim: `Store::approve` is marked `#[cfg(test)]` and only called by unit tests, while production uses `approve_with_context`.
invariant: Test suites should exercise the production `approve_with_context` API.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/observe.rs:488-510.
counterevidence: `#[cfg(test)]` prevents dead code in release builds, and several tests also test `approve_with_context` directly.

claim: `replace_candidate_with` allocates `to_lowercase()` at every char index and `preview()` checks candidate presence by replacing with `"\0"` and comparing strings.
invariant: String search in preview rendering can avoid per-character heap allocations.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/review.rs:248-256 and 736-746.
counterevidence: Context strings are bounded to 600 chars and only run on human preview requests.

claim: Hand-rolled CLI parser requires subcommand before global flags (e.g. `speech-front --lexicon PATH normalize` fails with `unknown command: --lexicon`) and treats misplaced flags like `--text` as positional text.
invariant: CLI parsers should reject unknown flags consistently rather than silently treating them as input text.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/main.rs:363-460 and reproduced during check-5 setup.
counterevidence: Documented CLI examples in README.md always place the subcommand first (`speech-front normalize --lexicon ...`).

claim: `candidates_by_kind` and `decisions` execute 4 secondary SQLite queries per row (N+1 query pattern).
invariant: Batching child lookups reduces query overhead for large limits.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/observe.rs:664-732 and 774-803.
counterevidence: SQLite runs in-process on local disk and default review queue limit is 10.

claim: `escape_attr` is a one-line wrapper identical to `escape_html`.
invariant: Trivial duplicate wrappers can be inlined unless distinct escaping rules are needed.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/review.rs:774-776.
counterevidence: `escape_html` already escapes `&`, `<`, `>`, `"`, and `'`, which is safe for quoted HTML attributes.

claim: `async fn decision` acquires a synchronous `std::sync::Mutex` (`state.decision_lock`) and holds it across synchronous SQLite I/O and `git commit` + `git push` subprocess execution on the Tokio worker thread.
invariant: Async HTTP handlers should use `spawn_blocking` (as `preview` already does at line 273) for blocking SQLite/filesystem/network-git operations.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/review.rs:135-191.
counterevidence: Review server binds to `127.0.0.1` for single-operator use.

claim: Review server router relies on Axum's default 2 MiB form body limit rather than setting a tighter `DefaultBodyLimit` (e.g. 16 KiB) for small decision/preview forms.
invariant: Explicit body limits proportional to form field bounds harden HTTP endpoints.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/review.rs:98-104.
counterevidence: Axum's built-in 2 MiB default already prevents unbounded memory allocation on loopback.

claim: `UnsupportedHtmlBlock` error response echoes the rejected HTML line inside JSON `{"error": "unsupported HTML block: ..."}`.
invariant: Error messages should bound or omit echoed user input.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/server.rs:472-473 and 534-535.
counterevidence: Response is `application/json` (escaped by `serde_json`), requires Bearer auth, and input is capped at 64 KiB.

claim: `read_text()` for CLI `normalize` and `observe` reads stdin via `read_to_string` without a `.take()` byte cap, unlike `russian-only` which caps stdin at 48,001 bytes (`main.rs:103`).
invariant: CLI stdin readers should bound input size consistently.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/main.rs:103 vs 507-513.
counterevidence: `normalize` and `observe` are local operator CLI commands, not network services.

claim: `ingest_text_path`, `ingest_conspects`, and `ingest_debriefs` call `fs::read_to_string` without checking file size metadata first.
invariant: Batch ingestion should skip or reject unexpectedly huge files before reading them into memory.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/ingest.rs:37,112,141.
counterevidence: Operator selects `--source PATH`, symlinks are skipped, and only `.md`/`.txt`/`.jsonl`/`.json` files are read.

claim: `open_regular_file` checks `fs::metadata(path)` before `options.open(path)` without `O_NOFOLLOW`.
invariant: Using `O_NOFOLLOW` on Linux closes the narrow TOCTOU symlink-swap window between path metadata check and open.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/lexicon_reload.rs:119-136.
counterevidence: `O_NONBLOCK` (0x800) prevents FIFO hangs on Linux, `file.metadata().is_file()` re-checks the opened descriptor at line 103, and the directory is trusted operator config (`docs/speech-front-integration.md:73-80`).

claim: `convert_with_deadline` polls child completion with `thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(5))` instead of blocking on `rx.recv_timeout(...)`.
invariant: Blocking channel wait with timeout avoids 5 ms polling latency and wakeups.
reason: Verified at teratts-server/src/russian_only.rs:218-244 (`rx.try_recv()` + `sleep(5ms)`).
counterevidence: Total deadline is 5s and admission control limits concurrent synthesis.

claim: CSRF token in `review.rs` is generated once per server process startup (192-bit random hex) rather than rotating per request/hour.
invariant: Loopback single-operator review server must prevent cross-origin form submission.
reason: Rejected as a defect: a 192-bit CSPRNG per-process token combined with `127.0.0.1` binding, `frame-ancestors 'self'`, `no-referrer`, and Origin/Host validation is completely sound for a single-operator local review tool.
counterevidence: Verified CSRF, Origin, Host, and CSP headers in `speech-front/src/review.rs`.

claim: Duplicate of G1-03: `parse_number` in `speech-front` lacks `followed_by_identifier_tail`, expanding `7-zip`, `12-factor`, `64-bit`.
invariant: Hyphenated number-word identifiers must not have their leading number expanded.
reason: Verified and reproduced in check-5; exact root-cause duplicate of G1-03.
counterevidence: Fixed in `teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:527`.

claim: Duplicate of G1-02: `speech-front` lacks `parse_iso_date`, turning `2026-08-12` into a range.
invariant: ISO-8601 dates must normalize as dates, not numeric ranges.
reason: Verified and reproduced in check-5; exact root-cause duplicate of G1-02.
counterevidence: Fixed in `teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:373-422`.

claim: Duplicate of G1-01: `speech-front` does not expand unit suffixes after decimal numbers (`2.5 км`).
invariant: Decimal numbers with unit abbreviations must expand and decline the unit.
reason: Verified and reproduced in check-5; exact root-cause duplicate of G1-01.
counterevidence: Fixed in `teratts-server/src/speechfront.rs:544-550`.

claim: Duplicate of G1-05: `teratts-server` dropped the leading-dot guard in `boundaries_match`.
invariant: Leading-dot lexicon entries must not match after path separators.
reason: Verified in check-4 diff; exact root-cause duplicate of G1-05.
counterevidence: `.NET` is not currently in `lexicon.toml`.

claim: `protect_numeric_plus` inserts `" плюс "` unconditionally, creating transient double spaces before `clean_spacing` collapses them.
invariant: Final normalized output must not contain double spaces.
reason: Rejected as a defect: as O2's own counterevidence notes, `clean_spacing` collapses all whitespace runs before returning, so final output has single spaces.
counterevidence: Unit test `protects_arithmetic_plus_without_changing_stress_or_cpp` passes.

claim: `normalize_symbols` converts `—` to `-` after `speechfront` range expansion.
invariant: Range separators must remain valid input to `speech-front` and downstream TTS.
reason: Rejected as a defect: explicitly documented at `server.rs:905` (`Number ranges can introduce typographic dashes after input preparation`) and benign.
counterevidence: Verified in `server.rs:905` and passing `russian_only` tests.

claim: Byte-level slicing in `russian_only.rs` relies on `char_indices()`/`len_utf8()` without a safety comment.
invariant: String slices must fall on UTF-8 character boundaries.
reason: Rejected as a defect: all byte offsets come directly from `char_indices()` and `len_utf8()` and are provably UTF-8 safe.
counterevidence: Verified by O2 and coordinator source inspection.

claim: `Store::open` configures no SQLite `busy_timeout` (default 0 ms), so any concurrent access during an active write/migration transaction immediately fails with `SQLITE_BUSY`.
invariant: SQLite connections shared across HTTP handlers and CLI commands should set a `busy_timeout`.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/observe.rs:129-133: no `busy_timeout` is set in production code.
counterevidence: Single-operator workload has low concurrency, though `index()`/`preview()` open new connections per request.

claim: `Store::initialize()` starts a `TransactionBehavior::Immediate` write transaction on every `Store::open()`, including read-only `index()`, `preview()`, and `candidates` calls on an already-migrated v3 database.
invariant: Read-only operations on an up-to-date schema should not acquire a write transaction on every connection open.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/observe.rs:144-256: `Transaction::new_unchecked(&self.0, TransactionBehavior::Immediate)` executes before checking `PRAGMA user_version == 3`.
counterevidence: The transaction is short-lived when `version == 3`, but amplifies `SQLITE_BUSY` risk when combined with O3-01.

claim: `publisher.publish()` runs after `approve_with_context` drops the `.speech-front.lock` file lock, allowing a concurrent CLI `approve` to modify `lexicon.toml` before `git add -- lexicon.toml`.
invariant: Git publish commits should capture only the lexicon state approved under the lock.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/observe.rs:544-661 and src/review.rs:183-192.
counterevidence: HTTP requests are serialized by `decision_lock`, and concurrent CLI + web approval by a single operator is rare.

claim: Duplicate of O1-01: `std::sync::Mutex` in `async fn decision` blocks Tokio executor thread across SQLite, file I/O, and `git push`.
invariant: Async handlers should offload blocking I/O and subprocesses via `spawn_blocking`.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/review.rs:131-196; exact root-cause duplicate of O1-01.
counterevidence: Single-operator loopback server.

claim: OS crash/power loss between atomic `lexicon.toml` rename and SQLite commit requires manual reconciliation using `.speech-front.backup`.
invariant: Cross-storage crash recovery boundaries must be documented and preserve backup files.
reason: Rejected as a defect: explicitly documented in `docs/pronunciation.md:126-129` and tested by `exclusive_recovery_files_and_external_edits_are_not_overwritten`.
counterevidence: Documented design invariant with non-destructive `.speech-front.backup` retention.

claim: `record`, `replace_source`, and `import_horizon` use `DEFERRED` transactions, which combined with 0 ms `busy_timeout` (O3-01) can fail with `SQLITE_BUSY` on upgrade to write lock.
invariant: Write transactions in `Store` should either use `IMMEDIATE` or rely on a non-zero `busy_timeout`.
reason: Verified at speech-front/src/observe.rs:260,313,380.
counterevidence: SQLite rolls back cleanly on `SQLITE_BUSY`, and setting `busy_timeout` (O3-01) resolves contention.

claim: `GitPublisher::publish()` verifies the active Git branch only at server startup (`new()`), not before each `git commit`.
